etymologies.etymologyHTML: From apology +‎ -ize, from ἀπολογία (apología, “a speech in defense”), from ἀπολογέομαι (apologéomai, “to speak in one’s defense”), from ἀπόλογος (apólogos, “an account, story”), compound of ἀπο- (apo-, “from, off”) and λόγος (lógos, “speech”); compare also ἀπολογίζομαι (apologízomai, “to render an account”).

definitions.definition: (intransitive, often followed by “for”) To make an apology or excuse; to acknowledge some fault or offense, with expression of regret for it, by way of amends

quote.citation: 1856, James Anthony Froude, History of England from the fall of Wolsey to the death of Elizabeth:
quote.text: Barnes was commanded, with Garrett and Jerome, to make a public acknowledgment of his errors; and to apologize especially for his insolent language to Gardiner

Today I want to apologize to my co-workers.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To express regret that a certain event has occurred.
(intransitive, dated) To make an apologia or defense; to act as apologist.

quote.citation: 1660, H[enry] More, An Explanation of the Grand Mystery of Godliness; […], London:  […]  J[ames] Flesher, for W[illiam] Morden […], →OCLC:
quote.text: To this purpose the most witty, cautious and subtile ſort of the Pagans apologize for themselves
